attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, part of his breakdown of the WSJ report. Not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement of a present-tense observation. The 'basically every major' scope is kept and nothing is added.

contract.note: The plain reading (leading LLMs of spring 2025 took both image and audio/voice input) is fair and ordinary. But the contract leaves open whether this means native model input or voice in the chatbot product, and the result depends on which one is used.

evidence.note: Meta's launch post for Llama 4 (April 2025) describes text and vision only, with no audio input. That makes one leading family an exception at the model level.

Dated the post day. OpenAI, Google and xAI chatbots offered voice chat, and Claude's voice mode, which handles images, was only starting a beta rollout. Supports the product-level reading for four families.
OpenAI's 2024 post says GPT-4o natively takes audio and image input. It is dated before the target period, so it counts as context only.
Google's December 2024 post says Gemini 2.0 Flash takes image and audio input. It is dated before the target period, so it counts as context only.
A report inferring that Claude relies on ElevenLabs for speech. It is about speech output and is an inference, so it does not settle whether Claude took native audio input.

reviews.rationale: Product-level reading: the packet shows voice input for OpenAI, Google, xAI and Claude (Claude only beginning beta on the post date), and says nothing on Meta's or DeepSeek's products. Native reading: Llama 4 lacks audio, and the packet does not establish Claude, Grok or DeepSeek. Neither the support condition (nearly all) nor the contradiction condition (several lacking) is clearly met, and the reading choice matters.
